propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate holds an active ISC2 CSSLP certification, first certified in March 2024 and checked on ISC2's member verification page.
propositions.rationale: The recruiter verification records a check of the member number against the issuing body's verification page.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate ran threat-modelling sessions with the gateway teams and recorded threats and agreed mitigations in the design tickets.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the sessions, the work sample shows one threat model and the reference confirms the work.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate prepared the secure-development evidence for the PCI DSS assessment and walked the assessor through it.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the assessment work and the former head of security engineering confirmed it.

expectedGap: Secure-coding guidance for TypeScript developers is not documented; the checklist covers Java services.
expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the register-checked CSSLP certification and the documented threat-modelling, scanning and PCI DSS work; do not extend the Java checklist into TypeScript guidance.
permittedFollowUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate has written or reviewed secure-coding guidance for TypeScript or front-end code.
